title: Transporting a bounded seek computation
statement: Let $Q,T,S$ be types with decidable equality, let $\mathrm{seek}$ be a two-work-tape Boolean machine with designated states $\mathrm{start},\mathrm{finish}$, and let $C$ be a natural number. Suppose that for every Boolean input $x$, natural number $p$, and Boolean word $w$, with $p\le |x|+1$, any configuration $c$ on $x$ in state $\mathrm{start}$ whose first work tape stores $w$ around its head at offsets $-1$ through $|w|$ and whose second tape is blank has a first arrival time $t\le C(|w|+c_{\mathrm{in}}+p+1)$ at state $\mathrm{finish}$. Until that time, both work-tape heads remain within distance $C(|w|+1)$ of their starting positions; at time $t$, the input-head position is $p$ and both tapes, both work-head positions, and the output are unchanged. Now let $\iota$ embed two work-tape indices into four, and let $d$ be a four-tape configuration over record symbols on the digit-embedded input, in state $\mathrm{start}$. Suppose every symbol stored on either embedded tape is a digit symbol, the first embedded tape stores the digit embedding of $w$ around its head at offsets $-1$ through $|w|$, and the second embedded tape is blank. Then the machine obtained by embedding the symbol-lifted seek machine has a first arrival at state $\mathrm{finish}$ at some time $t\le C(|w|+d_{\mathrm{in}}+p+1)$; its work-tape heads stay within distance $C(|w|+1)$ of their initial positions through time $t$, and at time $t$ the entire configuration is $d$ with state changed to $\mathrm{finish}$ and input-head position $p$.
